subject.title: fix(find): prevent recursive re-entry in child kill via sentinel guard (#98961)

question: Should maintainers require real OpenClaw find/fd process proof before merge, or accept this small sentinel-guarded lifecycle change from source review?
rationale: The external contributor's proof is terminal-style output and tests, but it does not inspectably run the patched OpenClaw find tool through the fd child-error path; only a maintainer should override that proof gate.

options.title: Require real find-path proof
options.body: Ask for redacted terminal output, logs, or a linked artifact that runs this branch through an fd spawn/error, abort, or kill-failure cleanup path before merge.

options.title: Accept source-level proof
options.body: A maintainer may explicitly accept the small guarded lifecycle change from source review and own the missing real-path proof risk.

options.title: Narrow the cleanup shape
options.body: Move the guarded stop call to only the child error path if maintainers do not want normal close cleanup to attempt the stop hook.

recommendation.title: Require real find-path proof
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted terminal output, logs, or a linked artifact that runs this branch through an fd spawn/error, abort, or kill-failure cleanup path before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete most recently landed related find subprocess lifecycle work in the same file and has the strongest current history signal for this proof-sufficiency choice.
